title: Getting Started with {poscosea}
text: poscosea provides fast sensitivity analysis posterior summaries obtained MCMC output. package implements infinitesimal jackknife (IJK) approximations based posterior draws scalar quantity interest, corresponding log-likelihood draws. influence values can used nonparametric bootstrap approximations, leave-k-cross-validation, sensitivity analysis without refitting original Bayesian model.

title: Getting Started with {poscosea}
text: package available GitHub. can install using remotes: using devtools:
code: install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("OhkuboYusaku/poscosea") install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("OhkuboYusaku/poscosea")

title: Getting Started with {poscosea}
text: main function requires numeric vector posterior draws (theta) log-likelihood matrix (loglik) Rows loglik correspond posterior draws theta columns correspond observations.
code: set.seed(123) n_obs <- 6 y <- rnorm(n_obs, sd = 1) # Introduce two influential observations. signal_idx <- c(2, 5) y[signal_idx] <- y[signal_idx] + 3  # Under y_i | theta ~ N(theta, 1) and a flat prior on theta, # theta | y is Normal(mean(y), 1 / n_obs). n_draws <- 2000 theta <- rnorm(n_draws, mean = mean(y), sd = 1 / sqrt(n_obs))  # Pointwise log-likelihood evaluated at the corresponding posterior draws. loglik <- matrix(0, n_draws, n_obs) for (i in seq_len(n_obs)) {   loglik[, i] <- dnorm(y[i], mean = theta, sd = 1, log = TRUE) }

title: Getting Started with {poscosea}
text: hierarchical count data analysed binomial N-mixture model, see vignette("nmix-twostage", package = "poscosea"), describes two-stage (site visit) bootstrap approximation implemented nmix_loglik(), ijk_nmix() ijk_bootstrap_2stage().

title: Two-Stage Bootstrap for N-Mixture Models
text: binomial N-mixture model, counts yijy_{ij} collected sites =1,…,Ii = 1, \ldots, repeated visits j=1,…,Jj = 1, \ldots, J: Ni∼Poisson(λi),yij∣Ni∼Binomial(Ni,pij).N_i \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_i), \qquad y_{ij} \mid N_i \sim \mathrm{Binomial}(N_i, p_{ij}). data hierarchical, bootstrap resample levels. two-stage bootstrap first resamples sites replacement, u∼Mult(;1/,…,1/)u \sim \mathrm{Mult}(; 1/, \ldots, 1/), resamples observed visits within selected copy site. Instead refitting model every resample, poscosea approximates replicate posterior mean single MCMC run: θ(b)≈E[θ]+∑(ubi−1)ci+∑,j(vbij−1)eij,\theta^{(b)} \approx E[\theta]   + \sum_{}(u_{bi} - 1)\, c_i   + \sum_{,j}(v_{bij} - 1)\, e_{ij}, cic_i eije_{ij} posterior covariances θ\theta site-level marginal log-likelihood visit-level log-likelihood, respectively. workflow nmix_draws() – pick λ\lambda, pp NN MCMC output, nmix_loglik() – compute site- visit-level log-likelihoods, ijk_nmix() – compute influence values quantity interest, ijk_bootstrap_2stage() – generate bootstrap replicates.

title: Two-Stage Bootstrap for N-Mixture Models
text: simulate data unmodelled overdispersion abundance, fitted Poisson N-mixture model misspecified.
code: set.seed(1) I <- 60; J <- 3 x  <- rnorm(I)                       # site covariate xp <- matrix(rnorm(I * J), I, J)     # visit covariate lambda_true <- exp(1.5 + 0.5 * x + rnorm(I, 0, 0.5)) N_true <- rpois(I, lambda_true) y <- matrix(rbinom(I * J, rep(N_true, J), plogis(0.5 * xp)), I, J) y[c(3, 10, 25), 3] <- NA             # some missing visits

title: Two-Stage Bootstrap for N-Mixture Models
text: practice parameter draws come MCMC (see last section). keep vignette self-contained, use Laplace normal approximation posterior (αλ,βλ,αp,βp)(\alpha_\lambda, \beta_\lambda, \alpha_p, \beta_p), independent weakly informative Normal priors specified . illustrative posterior draws, MCMC output. fitted Poisson model omits site-level abundance variation used generate data, resulting intervals read calibrated coverage results. draw NiN_i conditional posterior. nmix_loglik() accepts single draw evaluating marginal likelihood optimization.
code: prior_mean <- c(1.5, 0, 0, 0) prior_sd <- c(2, 1.5, 2, 2)  nll <- function(par) {   lam <- matrix(exp(par[1] + par[2] * x), 1)   p   <- matrix(plogis(par[3] + par[4] * xp), 1)   log_lik <- sum(suppressWarnings(nmix_loglik(y, lam, p)$site))   log_prior <- sum(dnorm(par, mean = prior_mean, sd = prior_sd, log = TRUE))   val <- -log_lik - log_prior   if (is.finite(val)) val else 1e10 } opt <- optim(c(1, 0, 0, 0), nll, method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE) if (opt$convergence != 0) stop("Posterior mode optimization did not converge.") post_cov <- solve(opt$hessian)  S  <- 2000 th <- t(opt$par + t(chol(post_cov)) %*% matrix(rnorm(4 * S), 4)) colnames(th) <- c("alpha.lam", "beta.lam", "alpha.p", "beta.p")  lambda <- exp(th[, 1] + outer(th[, 2], x))                   # S x I p      <- plogis(th[, 3] + outer(th[, 4], as.vector(xp)))    # S x IJ  ## N_i | y_i, theta on the grid max(y_i), ..., max(y_i) + 100 draw_N <- function(y, lambda, p, Nmax_extra = 100) {   S <- nrow(lambda); I <- nrow(y)   N <- matrix(NA_integer_, S, I)   for (i in seq_len(I)) {     obs <- which(!is.na(y[i, ]))     Ns  <- max(y[i, obs]) + 0:Nmax_extra     Nr  <- matrix(Ns, S, length(Ns), byrow = TRUE)     lt  <- dpois(Nr, lambda[, i], log = TRUE)     for (j in obs) lt <- lt + dbinom(y[i, j], Nr, p[, i + (j - 1) * I], log = TRUE)     cw <- t(apply(exp(lt - apply(lt, 1, max)), 1, cumsum))     N[, i] <- Ns[rowSums(cw < runif(S) * cw[, ncol(cw)]) + 1]   }   N } N <- draw_N(y, lambda, p)

title: Two-Stage Bootstrap for N-Mixture Models
code: fit_beta <- ijk_nmix(th[, "beta.lam"], ll) boot_two  <- ijk_bootstrap_2stage(fit_beta, type = "twostage", weights = w) boot_site <- ijk_bootstrap_2stage(fit_beta, type = "site", weights = w) boot_two #>  #> IJK Bootstrap Summary (N-mixture, type = "twostage") #>  #> Bootstrap replicates: 5000  #>  #>   estimate      bias   se lower upper #> 1    0.498 -5.33e-05 0.11 0.286 0.722 rbind(   posterior = c(estimate = mean(th[, "beta.lam"]), se = sd(th[, "beta.lam"]),                 setNames(quantile(th[, "beta.lam"], c(0.025, 0.975)), c("lower", "upper"))),   site      = unlist(summary(boot_site)[c("estimate", "se", "lower", "upper")]),   twostage  = unlist(summary(boot_two)[c("estimate", "se", "lower", "upper")]) ) #>            estimate         se     lower     upper #> posterior 0.4978255 0.08037342 0.3430796 0.6581175 #> site      0.4978255 0.10925440 0.2893603 0.7233496 #> twostage  0.4978255 0.11003653 0.2857569 0.7216042

title: Two-Stage Bootstrap for N-Mixture Models
text: matrix theta (draws rows, quantities columns) gives replicates quantities resamples.
code: xg <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 50) lam_curve <- exp(th[, "alpha.lam"] + outer(th[, "beta.lam"], xg))   # S x 50 fit_curve <- ijk_nmix(lam_curve, ll) sc <- summary(ijk_bootstrap_2stage(fit_curve, weights = w)) pq <- apply(lam_curve, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975))  plot(xg, sc$estimate, type = "n", ylim = range(sc$lower, sc$upper, pq),      xlab = "Site covariate", ylab = expression(lambda)) polygon(c(xg, rev(xg)), c(sc$lower, rev(sc$upper)), col = "grey80", border = NA) polygon(c(xg, rev(xg)), c(pq[1, ], rev(pq[2, ])), col = "grey55", border = NA) lines(xg, sc$estimate, lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("Two-stage bootstrap 95% CI", "Posterior 95% CrI"),        fill = c("grey80", "grey55"), border = NA, bty = "n")

title: Two-Stage Bootstrap for N-Mixture Models
text: JAGS (runjags), monitor λ\lambda, pp NN pass draws nmix_draws(). Columns matched name (lam[], p[,j], N[]), order output matter. detection model contains random effects, monitored pijp_{ij} conditional nmix_loglik() returns likelihood conditional random effects.
code: library(runjags) fit <- run.jags("Nmix.txt", monitor = c("beta", "lam", "p", "N"),                 data = jags_data, n.chains = 3) dr <- nmix_draws(as.mcmc.list(fit), I = nrow(y), J = ncol(y),                  lambda = "lam", p = "p", N = "N") ll <- nmix_loglik(y, dr$lambda, dr$p, N = dr$N)

what: A Computationally Efficient Sensitivity Analysis for MCMC Output
title: A Computationally Efficient Sensitivity Analysis for MCMC Output
text: poscosea provides infinitesimal jackknife (IJK) approximations sensitivity analysis posterior summaries. Given aligned posterior draws quantity interest pointwise log-likelihood values, computes observation-level influence values bootstrap leave-k-analyses. binomial N-mixture models, package also provides site- visit-level likelihood components two-stage bootstrap approximation. See N-mixture vignette worked example.

title: A Computationally Efficient Sensitivity Analysis for MCMC Output
text: Install development version GitHub:
code: install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("OhkuboYusaku/poscosea")

title: A Computationally Efficient Sensitivity Analysis for MCMC Output
text: example uses model y_i | theta ~ Normal(theta, 1) flat prior theta. draws resulting analytic posterior computes pointwise log-likelihood corresponding draw. Generate bootstrap replicates approximate leave-one-estimates: k must integer 1 number observations. Exhaustive leave-k-enumeration limited one million omission sets.
code: set.seed(123) n_obs <- 6 y <- rnorm(n_obs, sd = 1) signal_idx <- c(2, 5) y[signal_idx] <- y[signal_idx] + 3  n_draws <- 2000 theta <- rnorm(n_draws, mean = mean(y), sd = 1 / sqrt(n_obs)) loglik <- matrix(0, n_draws, n_obs) for (i in seq_len(n_obs)) {   loglik[, i] <- dnorm(y[i], mean = theta, sd = 1, log = TRUE) }  fit <- ijk(theta, loglik) fit$estimate head(fit$influence) boot <- ijk_bootstrap(fit$estimate, fit$influence, B = 500) summary(boot)  loo <- ijk_lko(fit$estimate, fit$influence, k = 1) plot(loo)

text: object object class "ijk_nmix". B Positive integer giving number bootstrap replicates weights NULL; ignored weights supplied. type One "twostage", "site", "visit". weights Optional weights nmix_weights(), share resamples across quantities. latent_resid Optional finite numeric vector (length \(S\)) finite numeric matrix \(S\) rows \(K\) columns, containing latent prediction errors; one randomly chosen draw added replicate.

title: Two-Stage Bootstrap Approximation for an N-Mixture Model — ijk_bootstrap_2stage
text: object class c("ijk_boot_nmix", "ijk_boot") estimate, replicates (vector length \(B\), \(B \times K\) matrix), B type.

title: Two-Stage Bootstrap Approximation for an N-Mixture Model — ijk_bootstrap_2stage
text: "twostage" Sites , within , visits resampled (see nmix_weights()). "site" sites resampled (\(v = 1\)); equivalent ijk_bootstrap() site-level influence. "visit" Sites kept (\(u = 1\)) visits resampled within site. quantity involves latent abundance , realised total \(\sum_i N_i\), likelihood-based replicates capture variation parameters. Pass latent_resid (see nmix_latent_resid()) add prediction error latent variables.

title: Two-Stage Bootstrap Approximation for an N-Mixture Model — ijk_bootstrap_2stage
code: set.seed(1) I <- 10; J <- 3; S <- 200 y <- matrix(rpois(I * J, 3), I, J) lambda <- matrix(rgamma(S * I, 20, 4), S, I) p <- matrix(runif(S * I * J, 0.4, 0.7), S, I * J) ll <- nmix_loglik(y, lambda, p) fit <- ijk_nmix(rowSums(lambda), ll) boot <- ijk_bootstrap_2stage(fit, B = 500) summary(boot) #>   estimate        bias       se  lower    upper #> 1 49.89695 -0.06030114 1.182523 47.621 52.15243

title: Infinitesimal Jackknife Influence for an N-Mixture Model — ijk_nmix
text: object class "ijk_nmix" containing estimate Posterior mean(s). influence_site Site-level influence values (centred, ijk()); vector length \(\), \(\times K\) matrix. influence_obs Observation-level influence values; length \(IJ\) (ordered \(+ (j-1)\)), 0 missing visits. obs_mask Observed-visit indicator. obs obs argument. site-level influence can passed ijk_lko() approximate leave-one-site-analysis.

title: Infinitesimal Jackknife Influence for an N-Mixture Model — ijk_nmix
text: first-order approximation posterior mean site weights \(u_i\) visit weights \(v_{ij}\) $$E_{u,v}[\theta] \approx E[\theta] + \sum_i (u_i - 1) c_i +       \sum_{,j} (v_{ij} - 1) e_{ij},$$ \(c_i = \mathrm{Cov}[\theta, \ell_i]\) (site-level marginal log-likelihood) \(e_{ij} = \mathrm{Cov}[\theta, \ell_{ij}]\) (observation-level log-likelihood).

title: Log-Likelihood Components of an N-Mixture Model — nmix_loglik
text: y Numeric counts \(\) rows (sites) \(J\) columns (visits); numeric vector treated one-column matrix. Counts must finite non-negative integers, except NA marks missing visit. Every site must least one observed visit. lambda Finite positive numeric matrix (\(S \times \)) posterior draws \(\lambda_i\); least one draw required. p Posterior draws \(p_{ij}\): either array (\(S \times \times J\)) matrix (\(S \times IJ\)) whose columns ordered \(k = + (j - 1) \) (column-major order used JAGS p[,j]). Values observed visits must finite 0 1; values missing visits used. N Optional numeric matrix (\(S \times \)) finite non-negative integer posterior draws \(N_i\); draw must least largest observed count site. Required obs_joint. Nmax_extra Non-negative integer; summation grid \(N_i\) extends Nmax_extra \(\max_j y_{ij}\).

title: Log-Likelihood Components of an N-Mixture Model — nmix_loglik
text: object class "nmix_loglik" containing site \(S \times \) matrix site-level marginal log-likelihoods. obs_rb \(S \times IJ\) matrix (see Details). Missing visits 0. obs_joint \(S \times IJ\) matrix NULL. condN \(S \times \) matrix \(E[N_i \mid y_i, \theta]\). obs_mask Logical \(\times J\) matrix, TRUE observed visits. tail_mass Largest conditional probability upper end grid; warning issued exceeds 1e-8.

title: Log-Likelihood Components of an N-Mixture Model — nmix_loglik
text: latent abundance \(N_i\) summed grid \(N = \max_j y_{ij}, \ldots, \max_j y_{ij} + \) Nmax_extra. Missing visits (NA y) dropped likelihood. observation-level log-likelihood returned two versions: obs_rb \(E[\log \mathrm{Bin}(y_{ij} \mid N, p_{ij}) \mid y_i, \theta]\), expectation conditional posterior \(N_i\). Use quantities depend parameters (e.g. regression coefficients, \(\lambda\)). smaller Monte Carlo noise. obs_joint \(\log \mathrm{Bin}(y_{ij} \mid N_i^{(s)}, p_{ij}^{(s)})\) evaluated posterior draws \(N_i\). Use quantities depend latent abundance (e.g. \(\sum_i N_i\)). available N supplied.

what: Two-Stage Bootstrap Weights for Site/Visit Data — nmix_weights
title: Two-Stage Bootstrap Weights for Site/Visit Data — nmix_weights
text: Draws bootstrap weights hierarchical data sites \(= 1, \ldots, \) visits \(j = 1, \ldots, J\). Sites resampled replacement, \(u \sim \mathrm{Mult}(; 1/, \ldots, 1/)\); , within selected copy site \(\), \(J_i\) observed visits resampled replacement, total weight visit \(j\) \(W_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Mult}(u_i J_i; 1/J_i, \ldots, 1/J_i)\) visit weight \(v_{ij} = W_{ij} / u_i\). Visits sites \(u_i = 0\) \(J_i = 1\), missing visits, get \(v_{ij} = 1\).
